decisions.reason: Product A builds directly on the firm's established messaging expertise and is supported by in-house R&D, so the firm can interpret results and improve it, making early withdrawal unlikely.

Product B extends the firm's established offer into document capture, which is related to its communication workflows, and the firm's own R&D enables learning and improvement, so it is likely to be kept.
Product C is closely tied to the firm's core email and fax conversion capabilities, and the firm's R&D supports assimilating feedback, so dropping it is unlikely.
Product D is a fax delivery optimization feature close to the firm's established offer, and given the firm's in-house R&D, it can be refined rather than dropped.
Product E builds on the firm's email security expertise and is supported by its R&D, allowing the firm to interpret results and continue improving the service.
